item.title: Can the 2025 Clean Competition Act Cut Global Emissions and Maintain U.S. Competitiveness?
item.description: The 2025 U.S. Clean Competition Act addresses the twin challenges of maintaining U.S. industrial competitiveness and accelerating industrial decarbonization by pairing a domestic performance fee with carbon import tariffs on carbon-intensive, trade-exposed sectors.

item.title: China Begins Relocating Structure from PMZ
item.description: CSIS imagery analysis and AIS data collection finds that China has begun relocating the Atlantic Amsterdam from inside the Provisional Measures Zone (PMZ) on January 27.

item.title: How Civil Society Exposes the Human Rights Risks of the Digital Silk Road
item.description: Emboldened authoritarian actors are no longer content to repress human rights in their own countries, but feel confident in their ability to share their tactics and technology across borders. Local civil society organizations stand at the front line against these mounting threats.

item.title: Deepening U.S.-Japan Economic Ties Through Workforce Development Cooperation
item.description: To successfully increase Japanese investment in the United States and strengthen U.S.-Japan economic cooperation, greater policy predictability and a shared approach to workforce development are critical.

item.title: What Does the Trump Administration’s New National Defense Strategy Say About China?
item.description: The Trump administration released its long-awaited National Defense Strategy on January 23. Here is how to interpret what the strategy says about China.

item.title: Rethinking Comparative Advantage
item.description: This week, Bill Reinsch explores comparative advantage, the difficulty of building competitive sectors today, and why cooperation with other countries is essential.

item.title: Japanese Energy Companies Step Up U.S. Investments
item.description: The series of major Japanese investments in U.S. gas assets since last year is driven by commercial, policy, and geopolitical factors.
